description:
*Warning:  potentially harrowing and dismal content above*
.
.
media (after cover image) are in chronological order

2022 May 08
A large cactus next to the house front door had a nest with three roadrunner babies.
I stepped out and happened to notice a large gopher snake on the ground inside the chickenwire enclosure, trying to swallow a roadrunner (baby or adult?).  The snake appeared stretched to the limit.  Two roadrunner babies were also down on the ground, trying not to be noticed.  I guessed that the snake either would leave the scene afterwards or else a parent would return and attack the snake, and I decided not to interfere.  Instead, the snake apparently Regurgitated the first roadrunner back by the wall (#10 #11), and then killed a Second baby and apparently swallowed that one. (#7)  Seeing that the babies were like fish in a barrel (and not using the board ramp), we immediately pulled up the chickenwire so the last baby could escape, which it probably did after we rushed back in the house.

A parent bird returned, came into the enclosure and called to the dead regurgitated roadrunner, but it didn't attack the snake. (#8 #9)  Maybe it thought it was outclassed by that size of snake?  The parent just stood there and looked and made some calls, from a few feet away.  The snake was seen in the yard the next morning and I'm told it was long... 7-8ft?

One lesson here is that baby birds under pressure aren't smart enough to go to a ramp. If bird babies ever show up there again, that chickenwire will have to be pulled up to allow for fast getaways.
